question.prompt:
Six regular hexagons surround a regular hexagon of side length \(1\) as shown. What is the area of \(\triangle{ABC}?\)

[Figure 1](figures/2014_AMC_10B_Q13_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
Use \(BC\) as the base and find the horizontal distance from \(A\) to it. Every surrounding hexagon also has side length \(1\), because it shares a whole side with the central hexagon.

Joining the center of a regular hexagon to its vertices divides it into six congruent triangles with central angle \(360^\circ/6=60^\circ\). These triangles are equilateral, so the center-to-vertex distance is also \(1\). An altitude of a unit equilateral triangle bisects its base and has length
\[
h=\sqrt{1^2-\left(\frac12\right)^2}
=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}.
\]
Thus, in the displayed orientation, a hexagon's opposite left and right vertices are \(2\) units apart. Its upper-left and lower-left vertices are vertically aligned and separated by \(2h=\sqrt3\).

Let \(D\) and \(E\) be the leftmost and rightmost vertices of the central hexagon. The segment \(AD\) is a side of an outer hexagon, so \(AD=1\). At \(D\), the \(120^\circ\) angle of the upper-left hexagon and the \(60^\circ\) angle of a central equilateral triangle add to \(180^\circ\). Hence \(AD\) continues the central diagonal \(DE\), giving
\[
AE=AD+DE=1+2=3.
\]
In the upper-right hexagon, \(B\) and \(E\) are its upper-left and lower-left vertices. In the lower-right hexagon, \(E\) and \(C\) occupy the corresponding positions. Consequently, \(B,E,C\) lie on a vertical line and
\[
BC=BE+EC=\sqrt3+\sqrt3=2\sqrt3.
\]
The horizontal segment \(AE\) is perpendicular to \(BC\), so it is the required altitude. Therefore
\[
[\triangle ABC]
=\frac12\cdot BC\cdot AE
=\frac12\cdot2\sqrt3\cdot3
=\boxed{3\sqrt3},
\]
choice \(\mathrm B\).
solutions.title: Measure the base and height through the hexagons
